amendments.text: Pilot (3 candidate instances, 4 seeds x harden/rigid each, run before plan commit): all three DISCRIMINATE strongly but rigid wins on all: p1-wide18 (n=18, w/h [0.4,2.6]) margin -0.3308; p2-extreme20 (n=20, 3x[2.2,3.0]+17x[0.2,0.5]) margin -0.1509; p3-aspect16 (n=16, w[0.3,2.4] h[0.3,1.2]) margin -0.1676. Margins far exceed the 0.01 discrimination bar. Direction (rigid wins) is a finding, not a design flaw: the fidelity decision rule tests harden's gap to optimum, not head-to-head wins. Full instance set built around these three archetypes plus medium-wide and tall-skinny variants for shape-variance coverage.

decision_rule: Spearman(fidelity, harden_gap) < -0.3 with one-sided p < 0.05 across the 18 instances -> the scaffold-fidelity rule TRANSFERS on hard heterogeneous instances. Otherwise it does not transfer on hard instances (null preserved). Descriptively: harden win rate vs H01's 2/10, and whether rigid's pilot advantage replicates at 16 seeds.
fidelity_measure: Frozen from H01 / when-hardening-helps A12/C13/C17: scaffold = pairwise centroid-distance ordering at compress-end (last 'compress' frame) of the best-L harden run; reference = best-known optimum arrangement (lowest L across both methods and all seeds); fidelity = Spearman rho between the two distance orderings; harden_gap = best harden L - best-known L.
hypothesis: On heterogeneous instances hard enough to discriminate (harden vs rigid margins >> 0.01), the scaffold-fidelity rule transfers: higher scaffold fidelity predicts a smaller gap between hardening's best result and the best-known optimum.
instance_notes: Uniform instances use engine genPieces({n, w:[lo,hi], h:[lo,hi]}, pseed). Bimodal instances compose genPieces({n: n_large, w: large, h: large}, pseed) ++ genPieces({n: n_small, w: small, h: small}, pseed+1000); large pieces listed first. Archetypes: A=wide uniform (area ~40x), B=extreme bimodal (few huge + many tiny), C=aspect-ratio mix (flat + square), D=medium-wide uniform (bridge to H01 scale), E=moderate bimodal, F=tall-skinny mix. All deterministic given pseed.
question: When heterogeneous instances are hard enough that harden and rigid produce clearly different results, does the disk scaffold's arrangement still predict hardening's outcome?
title: Does the scaffold-fidelity rule transfer on hard heterogeneous instances?
